articles.kicker: Last in the league, and the only owner whose opening night actually went to plan
articles.title: The Hawks Tagged Patrick Mahomes in May and Opened the Season Without Him
articles.dek: Chris Klingenberg began April with 0 top-twelve players and no quarterback at all. He nearly doubled his lineup value at the auction and still ranks 12 of 12 with 5 holes.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: Lowest auction spend in the league, one trade all year, fourth in the table
articles.title: Cleon Ca$h Let the Draft Do His Offseason and It Worked
articles.dek: Eric Mannila spent $34,000 at auction — less than anybody — made 1 trade, and ranks 4 of 12. The pick at 1.01 did more for this roster than his entire summer of shopping.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: The biggest cheque in the league, and a defensive front that cost almost nothing
articles.title: Blake Bombers Paid a Record Price for Josh Allen and Got the Rest of the Roster for Free
articles.dek: Shawn Blake spent $88,000 on one quarterback — the most expensive lot anybody won all summer and 68.2% of his own auction budget. He ranks 3 of 12 and his best defender is on a minimum contract.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: Best roster in the league, and a defense assembled entirely from the clearance rack
articles.title: C-Town Chivalry Sold Its Mistakes to the League and Bought a Champion With the Proceeds
articles.dek: Bear Dunn ranks 1 of 12 with 0 holes and 6 studs. He got there by releasing two expensive players in July and watching other owners pay almost the same money for them weeks later.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: The hardest-working defense in the league, assembled entirely out of other people's leftovers
articles.title: Real Deal Creel Bought a Superstar and Shoplifted the Rest
articles.dek: Keith Creelman spent $189,000 at the Free Agent Auction and 7.1% of his money on defense. Real Deal Creel came out 7 of 12. Both of those are on purpose.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: He tagged Christian McCaffrey in May and cut him in July, and it was the right call
articles.title: Sex Manther Tore Down a Contender in Three Days and Rebuilt a Better One
articles.dek: Josh Martel went into the auction carrying $103,000 of salary, down from $277,000 in April. He released two of the most expensive players in the league in the same week and used the money on the best quarterback room anybody has.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: The cheapest elite defense ever assembled, and one very expensive receiver
articles.title: The Long Haulers Got Paid to Take a Franchise Quarterback and Built a Defense Out of Loose Change
articles.dek: Brian Cross put 71.8% of his auction money into defenders — the largest share in the league — and his most expensive buy all summer was $8,000. He ranks 6 of 12 and has 6 studs, which is as many as anyone.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: Elite at receiver, elite at tight end, elite on defence, and starting a wide receiver at quarterback
articles.title: HammerTime Sold Jalen Hurts in April and Has Been Playing a Man Short Ever Since
articles.dek: Eric Martel traded a starting quarterback for picks, spent the picks on running backs, and now ranks 12 of 12 at the position. Everything else on this roster is very good, which is what makes it hurt.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: The only roster in the league that never had a hole in it, at any point, all year
articles.title: Pure Greatness Spent the Offseason Doing Almost Nothing, Which Was the Correct Answer
articles.dek: Brian Cutting entered April with 0 holes in his priced lineup, entered the auction with 0, and came out with 0. He ranks 2 of 12 and the most expensive player he bought all summer is on his bench.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: He won the biggest trade of the offseason and then bought a quarterback he did not need
articles.title: Gride Landed Amon-Ra St. Brown, Cash, and Eleventh Place
articles.dek: Matt Gerardi took the best player in the summer's biggest trade and got paid $10,000 to do it. He still ranks 11 of 12, because he spent almost everything else on the one position he had already solved.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: Nine players in April, no money in August, and still no quarterback
articles.title: CBP Bought Every Running Back in the Building and Forgot the Position That Matters
articles.dek: Derrick Whitman entered the offseason with 9 active players and left the auction with 1 hole in a starting lineup. It cost him $172,000 and every dollar of cap room he had.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: First in the league at the thing nobody drafts for, last in the division at everything else
articles.title: L.A. Looks Fielded the Best Defense in the League and Sold the Offense to Pay for It
articles.dek: Ryan Bousquet ranks 1 of 12 in points per started defender and 10 of 12 overall. In between those two numbers is a July trade that sent his best receiver out the door one day before the roster locked.

sections.title: Contracts, Trades, Cuts and the Rookie Class

articles.kicker: Nobody left the auction quietly
articles.title: Everybody Paid. Somebody Overpaid.
articles.dek: Eric Mannila spent less than anyone and came out with one of the best offenses in the league; Keith Creelman spent more than anyone and did not.

articles.kicker: A perfect week, spent on nothing
articles.title: Klingenberg Beat Everybody, and the Only Race That Moved Was the Ugly One
articles.dek: The biggest score in the league belonged to an eliminated team, and the entire week resolved into a straight swap between Keith Creelman and Shawn Blake for a division bid neither of them has earned.

articles.kicker: The best week of anyone's season landed in the wrong bracket.
articles.title: Outgunned, Not Outmanaged
articles.dek: Eric Mannila beat every roster in the league on a weekend it could no longer buy him anything, and Brian Cutting quietly took the whole thing.

articles.kicker: Round one, and only the cellar-bound had an excuse
articles.title: The Beaten and the Self-Beaten
articles.dek: Eric Martel outscored the entire league, Trevor Lawrence had the game of his season in a match that decided nothing, and the four losers sorted themselves into unlucky and unforgivable.

articles.kicker: Nobody set a bad lineup. Plenty of people lost anyway.
articles.title: Bear Dunn Beat Everybody
articles.dek: Josh Allen produced the day of the week, the only careless lineups belonged to men it did not cost, and not one loser can blame his bench.

articles.kicker: The bracket thins out
articles.title: The Losers Who Started Ghosts
articles.dek: Every man who lost a game he could have won had a starter who never took the field, and the title is down to two housemates.
